plan.notes: Source: University of Connecticut School of Engineering 'Computer Science (BS) Catalog Year 2026-2027' Common Map (Storrs), https://advising-engineering.media.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3638/2026/05/CS-26-27-Common-Map.pdf. Degree name verified on catalog.uconn.edu ('Computer Science (BS)', Bachelor of Science, School of Engineering). This is the official recommended term-by-term sequence for the Engineering BS; UConn Stamford publishes a separate variant — this plan targets Storrs. The map is explicitly a 'recommended sequence' and notes shifts may occur due to prereq completion/course availability. Transcription method: direct term-by-term transcription of the official PDF; no courses, credits, or prerequisites invented. Course titles for fixed courses verified against the catalog.uconn.edu 'Computer Science (BS)' catalog page (which also publishes the 120-credit degree total). Choice slots: TOI = UConn Topical Inquiry general-education courses (three 3-credit courses in the sequence). 'Lab Science' slots = the catalog's 8-credit two-semester laboratory science sequence (Chemistry/Physics pairs) plus the 4-credit additional science course, all shown as three 4-credit choice slots in semesters 1-3 per the map. 'CSE Elective 3000+ or Concentration Course' = catalog rule: concentration students take the required + elective courses of a concentration (each 12 credits); students with no concentration take 12 credits of 3000+ CSE beyond required courses. 'Probability & Statistics Course' = one of MATH 3160, STAT 3025Q, STAT 3345Q, STAT 3375Q per the official catalog page. The final free-elective slot is '1+ credits, as needed to reach total degree credits' — recorded as 1 credit. Prerequisites: the Common Map does not list course prerequisites, so no prereq codes were attached (never invented). ENGR 1000 'Orientation to Engineering' is 1 credit. CSE 3000 is 1 credit. CSE 4939W is the W-designated (writing-intensive) capstone course.
